domain: For each workload, all recorded calendar days in its selected full year, aligned to midnight. The finite reference domain and calibration are fixed before selecting a released day; all distinct days in that domain are adjacent.
privacy_unit: One whole day. All publications and adaptive postprocessing queries for that day's mechanism share its total budget. No annual or person-level guarantee is asserted.
calibration: Take the maximum over every pair of dates in the same workload, including different months. Never choose a noise scale using only the particular released day.
boundary: Reset signal history and Brownian path at midnight. Query windows remain within the day. Source local-clock coordinates retained for travel data; UTC for USGS.
hard: One independent Gaussian release per completed T-bin; N=floor(86400/T), epsilon/N and delta/N. Compute each (T,w) window-vector L1 maximum and verify it covers every published scalar bin difference. The final incomplete bin has no release.
brownian: Compute the exact maximum smoothed-rate squared-difference integral over every within-day w-window and every pair of days, for each (w,tau). Cover the entire day when calibrating a continuous path; a window bound alone is not a whole-day privacy bound. Separate calibrated configurations must not be composed for free.
grid: Same released Brownian path and noise scale as continuous; at time s return the cached increment with endpoints floor(s/T)T and (floor(s/T)-floor(w/T))T. No fresh off-grid information. Evaluate all three methods on the identical query set; additionally report on-grid queries separately.
metrics: Per-day expected MSE and expected relative error on positive-truth queries; report zero-truth fraction separately. Macro average across days. All three methods appear in every comparison table and figure.
data: Reuse retained original downloads and normalized monthly arrays. Preserve source hashes, daily arrays, all calibration witnesses, per-day metrics, and standalone plotting scripts with their input CSVs. No downloads needed.
